comparison: Perfect agreement on behavioral validation claims (C27-C33). Both evaluations find these task performance metrics well-supported. OpenEval provides detailed statistical justification while peer reviewers implicitly accept these foundational results as sound.

Perfect agreement on systematic behavioral differences in one dataset (C34-C36). Both evaluations accept the observed difference and the plausible explanation provided by the authors regarding task design variations.

Perfect agreement on reliability conclusions (C69-C70). Both evaluations support the claim that consistency across 7T datasets demonstrates reliability, though OpenEval notes the caveat that consistency alone doesn't guarantee validity.

Substantial agreement on error processing interpretation (C78-C84), but with different levels of certainty. OpenEval rates these claims as UNCERTAIN due to their speculative nature, while peer reviewers appear to accept the interpretative framework without explicit challenge.

Strong agreement on literature characterization (C23-C26 in OpenEval; C23-C26, C85 in peer review). Both evaluations accept the authors' summary of inconsistent fMRI findings and the contextualization within prior meta-analyses.

Strong agreement on tSNR findings (C37-C40). Both evaluations accept the data quality assessments and 7T advantages. OpenEval provides detailed technical justification while peer reviewers implicitly accept these through characterizing the study as 'well-powered.'

Strong agreement on methodological caveats about subcortical BOLD signals (C71-C76). Both evaluations accept these important limitations. OpenEval emphasizes their role in explaining discrepancies with other modalities.

Strong agreement on foundational background claims (C1-C10 in OpenEval; C1-C22 in peer review). Both evaluations find these well-established concepts appropriately cited and supported. Peer review covers broader background including neural pathways.

Strong agreement on neural pathway literature (C11-C21). Both evaluations accept these claims as appropriately supported by prior research. OpenEval provides detailed assessment while peer reviewers acknowledge the established framework.

Agreement on smoothing effects (C58-C59). Both evaluations accept the dramatic differences shown in preprocessing approaches. Peer review groups this with broader methodological claims (C87, C89, C90).

Agreement on methodological considerations (C87-C90). Both evaluations support these analysis approach claims. OpenEval emphasizes empirical support from smoothing comparison while peer reviewers accept the overall methodological framework.

Agreement on technical limitations of fMRI for subcortical imaging (C65-C68). Both evaluations accept these contextual claims about spatial resolution and coverage. OpenEval highlights their importance for interpretation.

Agreement on main voxel-wise fMRI results (C43-C46). Both evaluations support these findings. Peer review groups these with broader results including ROI analyses, while OpenEval separates voxel-wise from ROI-wise findings.
Agreement on FS > GO ROI results (C47-C50). Both evaluations support these detailed findings. Peer review integrates these with other contrasts in comprehensive assessment of main findings.
Agreement on FS > SS ROI results (C51-C53). Both evaluations support the convergence between frequentist and Bayesian approaches. Peer review groups with broader results assessment.

Agreement on critical SS > GO results (C54-C57). Both evaluations support the finding of limited subcortical activation during successful stopping and the Bayesian evidence for null effects. This represents a major finding of the study.

Agreement on main conclusions (C60-C64). Both evaluations support these claims. OpenEval notes appropriate framing as suggestions rather than definitive proof, while peer reviewers affirm 'solid evidence for conclusions.'

Agreement on overall conclusions (C91-C93). Both evaluations support the main findings about activation patterns. OpenEval notes C94 is speculative but rates overall as SUPPORTED; peer reviewers accept the framework.
Agreement on contextualization with prior meta-analyses (C85). Both evaluations accept this claim as appropriately supported by citations to three prior meta-analyses showing similar findings.

Agreement on novelty claim (C86), but with different levels of certainty. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to inability to verify comprehensiveness of literature search, while peer reviewers accept the claim without challenge.

Agreement on methodological inference (C88). Both evaluations accept this claim. OpenEval groups it with broader methodological considerations while peer reviewers include it with novelty and speculative claims.

Agreement on speculative mechanistic claim (C94). OpenEval explicitly notes this is speculative but rates overall result as SUPPORTED; peer reviewers accept without challenge, suggesting acceptance of the hypothesis.
